title: Vanishing above the dimension of a curve
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be a
curve over $k$ which is smooth and
projective. For every
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module $\mathcal{F}$ one has

$$
H^i(X,\mathcal{F})=0\qquad\text{for all }i\ge2 .
$$

(EGA III$_1$, (3.2.1): cohomology of a Noetherian scheme of
dimension $d$ vanishes above $d$; here $d=1$.)

proof.text: By [def-pc-smooth-projective-curve] and [def-pc-curve], the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is of finite type. Since $k$ is a field, $\operatorname{Spec}(k)$ is Noetherian; therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] implies that $X$ is a Noetherian scheme.

source.place: Lemma 01T6 (finite type over a Noetherian scheme)

proof.text: The curve hypothesis gives $\dim X=1$ as the supremum of the dimensions of its local rings [def-pc-curve, def-pc-dimension]. By [lem-pc-scheme-dimension-local-rings], this equals the topological Krull dimension of the underlying space, so $\operatorname{topologicalKrullDim}(X)=1$.

For $q\ge2$, the equality $\operatorname{topologicalKrullDim}(X)=1$ gives $\operatorname{topologicalKrullDim}(X)<q$. Applying [lem-sc-noetherian-cohomology-above-dimension] to the Noetherian scheme $X$ and the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F$ yields $H^q(X,\mathcal F)=0$ for every $q\ge2$.
